researcher_only: Never copy into an agent image, container, workspace, prompt, tool result or the conference library.
written: 2026-10-20, by the implementing development agent, from the pinned Lean statements (data/manifest.json, data/templates/) and docs/problems.md; not separately reviewed by the owner.
rule: One neutral sentence per task saying what the pinned statement asks, in everyday words. No status, known answer, solution or difficulty. A task without a sentence (plain null) is named by its title only.
used_by: research/analysis/judge/tasks_plain.py: the TASKS IN PLAIN WORDS section of the candidate, verifier and run-level requests (context, not evidence) and the 'Problem' lines of report.html and the evidence browser.

Buchi_buchi_false_M4.title: Büchi's problem — buchi_false_M4
Buchi_buchi_false_M4.plain: Show that a property from Büchi's problem fails for 4: there are integers x and a, with a not zero, such that (x + n)^2 + a is a perfect square for each of n = 0, 1, 2 and 3.

DedekindNumber_M'_three.title: Dedekind Numbers — M'_three
DedekindNumber_M'_three.plain: Show that there are exactly 20 'antichains' of subsets of a three-element set: collections of subsets in which no member is contained in another, the empty collection included.

Erdos1059_allFactorialSubtractionsCompos.title: Erdős Problem 1059 — allFactorialSubtractionsComposite_101
Erdos1059_allFactorialSubtractionsCompos.plain: Show that 101 minus any factorial smaller than 101 (that is, 101 - 1, 101 - 2, 101 - 6 and 101 - 24) is a composite number, not a prime.

Erdos1074_erdos_1074_variants_EHSNumbers.title: Erdős Problem 1074 — erdos_1074.variants.EHSNumbers_init
Erdos1074_erdos_1074_variants_EHSNumbers.plain: Show that the first seven numbers m of a certain kind (those for which some prime p divides m! + 1, m factorial plus one, while p does not leave remainder 1 on division by m) are 8, 9, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17.

Erdos1085_erdos_1085_variants_upper_d3.title: Erdős Problem 1085 — erdos_1085.variants.upper_d3
Erdos1085_erdos_1085_variants_upper_d3.plain: Let f(n) be the largest number of pairs at distance exactly 1 that n points in three-dimensional space can have; decide whether f(n) is at most a constant times n^(4/3) times log log n for all large n.

Erdos1092_f_asymptotic_2.title: Erdős Problem 1092 — f_asymptotic_2
Erdos1092_f_asymptotic_2.plain: For graphs on n points the file defines f(2, n), roughly the largest k such that a graph is guaranteed to be 3-colourable whenever each of its subgraphs can be made 3-colourable by deleting at most k edges; decide whether f(2, n) grows faster than n itself.

Erdos141_exists_three_consecutive_primes.title: Erdős Problem 141 — exists_three_consecutive_primes_in_ap
Erdos141_exists_three_consecutive_primes.plain: Show that some three consecutive prime numbers are evenly spaced: the gap from the first to the second equals the gap from the second to the third.

Erdos195_erdos_195_variants_leq_5_bound.title: Erdős Problem 195 — erdos_195.variants.leq_5_bound
Erdos195_erdos_195_variants_leq_5_bound.plain: Show that 5 bounds the length k for which every reshuffling of all the integers (a one-to-one rearrangement) is guaranteed to contain, at increasing positions, k values forming an evenly spaced increasing or decreasing sequence, as the file defines this largest guaranteed length.

Erdos23_erdos_23_variants_n1_tight.title: Erdős Problem 23 — erdos_23.variants.n1_tight
Erdos23_erdos_23_variants_n1_tight.plain: Show that there is a graph on 5 points with no triangle whose points cannot be split into two groups with every edge running between the groups, so that at least one edge would have to be removed to allow such a split.

Erdos340_greedySidon_go_singleton_two.title: Erdős Problem 340 — greedySidon_go_singleton_two
Erdos340_greedySidon_go_singleton_two.plain: Show that one step of the file's greedy construction picks 2: starting from the set {1}, the smallest number that is at least 2, not already in the set, and keeps all sums of two members different is 2.

Erdos56_maxWeaklyDivisible_one.title: Erdős Problem 56 — maxWeaklyDivisible_one
Erdos56_maxWeaklyDivisible_one.plain: Show that, for every positive k, the largest set of numbers chosen from 1 to 1 in which no k + 1 members are pairwise without common factors has exactly 1 element.

Erdos699_sylvester_schur.title: Erdős Problem 699 — sylvester_schur
Erdos699_sylvester_schur.plain: Show that whenever 1 <= i <= n/2, the binomial coefficient 'n choose i' (the number of ways to pick i things out of n) has a prime factor larger than i.

Erdos6_erdos_6_variants_decreasing.title: Erdős Problem 6 — erdos_6.variants.decreasing
Erdos6_erdos_6_variants_decreasing.plain: Show that, for every chosen length, there are infinitely many places in the list of prime numbers where that many consecutive gaps between neighbouring primes keep getting strictly smaller, each gap smaller than the one before.

EulerBrick_cuboidThree.title: Open questions regarding the existence of Euler bricks — cuboidThree
EulerBrick_cuboidThree.plain: Show that, for every three distinct positive whole numbers a, b and c with no common factor shared by all three (excluding the cases b x c = a^2 and a x c = b^2), a specific degree-12 polynomial built from a, b and c cannot be factored into smaller polynomials with integer coefficients; the statement is linked to the search for a box whose edges and diagonals all have whole-number lengths.

GRH_implies_riemannHypothesis.title: Riemann Hypothesis and its generalizations — implies_riemannHypothesis
GRH_implies_riemannHypothesis.plain: Show that the simplest special case of the generalized Riemann hypothesis (the case of modulus 1) says the same thing as the classical Riemann hypothesis about where the zeros of the zeta function lie: a check that the general statement is set up correctly.

Green14_W_3_11.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 14 — W_3_11
Green14_W_3_11.plain: Show that W(3, 11) = 114, where W(3, 11) is the smallest N such that, however the numbers 1 to N are coloured red and blue, there is a red evenly spaced run of 3 numbers or a blue evenly spaced run of 11.

Green32_hasCosetHole_empty.title: Green's Open Problem 32 — hasCosetHole_empty
Green32_hasCosetHole_empty.plain: A basic check of a definition used for Green's Problem 32: show that, among strings of n zeros and ones, the empty set has a 'coset hole' of size 0 in the sense defined in the file (a shifted subspace that it misses).

Green38_green_38_test_zero_mem_validCard.title: Green's Open Problem 38 — green_38.test_zero_mem_validCardinalities
Green38_green_38_test_zero_mem_validCard.plain: A basic check of a definition used for Green's Problem 38: show that 0 is one of the allowed set sizes in the file's definition (the empty set satisfies its condition).

MagicSquares_exists_semi_magic_square_cu.title: Magic Squares — exists_semi_magic_square_cubes
MagicSquares_exists_semi_magic_square_cu.plain: Decide whether nine different cubes of positive whole numbers can be placed in a 3-by-3 grid so that every row and every column adds up to the same total.

MonochromaticQuantumGraph_eqSystem10_no_.title: Monochromatic quantum graphs (inherited vertex colorings) — eqSystem10_no_solution_d9

OeisA287616_conjecture.title: Sum of a triangular number, a generalized pentagonal number, and a generalized heptagonal number — conjecture

SumOfThreeCubes_isSumOfThreeCubes_iff_mo.title: Sum of three cubes — isSumOfThreeCubes_iff_mod_9
SumOfThreeCubes_isSumOfThreeCubes_iff_mo.plain: Decide whether an integer can be written as a sum of three integer cubes (x^3 + y^3 + z^3, negative numbers allowed) exactly when it does not leave remainder 4 or 5 on division by 9.

Transcendental_exp_mul_pi_transcendental.title: Open questions on transcendence of numbers — exp_mul_pi_transcendental
Transcendental_exp_mul_pi_transcendental.plain: Show that the number e times pi is transcendental: it is not a root of any nonzero polynomial with rational coefficients.

WrittenOnTheWallII_GraphConjecture16_con.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 16 — conjecture16

WrittenOnTheWallII_Test_C6_avg_dist.title: Testing Graph Invariants — C6_avg_dist
WrittenOnTheWallII_Test_C6_avg_dist.plain: Show that in a ring of six points (each point joined to its two neighbours), the average distance between two different points, counted in steps around the ring, is 9/5.

WrittenOnTheWallII_Test_C6_size.title: Testing Graph Invariants — C6_size
WrittenOnTheWallII_Test_C6_size.plain: Show that a ring of six points, each point joined to its two neighbours, has exactly 6 connections (edges).

WrittenOnTheWallII_Test_Star5_indep.title: Testing Graph Invariants — Star5_indep
WrittenOnTheWallII_Test_Star5_indep.plain: Show that in a star made of one centre point joined to five outer points, the largest group of points with no two of them joined has 5 points.

WrittenOnTheWallII_Test_house_cvetkovic.title: Testing Graph Invariants — house_cvetkovic
WrittenOnTheWallII_Test_house_cvetkovic.plain: Show that for the 'house' graph (five points drawn as a square with a triangular roof), a number computed from the eigenvalues of its connection table (the count of zero eigenvalues plus the smaller of the counts of positive and negative ones) equals 3.

all_fermat_squarefree.title: Open questions about Fermat numbers — all_fermat_squarefree
all_fermat_squarefree.plain: Decide whether every Fermat number (2 raised to the power 2^n, plus 1: 3, 5, 17, 257, 65537, ...) is squarefree, meaning that no square of a whole number larger than 1 divides it.

catalan_conjecture.title: Catalan's conjecture and related Diophantine equations — catalans_conjecture
catalan_conjecture.plain: Show that the only way two powers of positive whole numbers, each with an exponent of at least 2, can differ by exactly 1 (x^a - y^b = 1) is 3^2 - 2^3 = 1.

erdos_1064.title: Erdős Problem 1064 — erdos_1064
erdos_1064.plain: Show that for almost all whole numbers n (a set of density 1), phi(n) > phi(n - phi(n)), where phi(n) counts the numbers from 1 to n that share no factor with n.

erdos_18a.title: Erdős Problem 18 — erdos_18a
erdos_18a.plain: Decide whether, for infinitely many 'practical' numbers m (numbers whose divisors can be added up to make every whole number from 1 to m), every number from 1 to m can be written as a sum of distinct divisors of m using very few of them: fewer than a fixed power of log log m.

erdos_400_part_i.title: Erdős Problem 400 — erdos_400.parts.i
erdos_400_part_i.plain: For each k of at least 2, let g(n) measure how far a1 + ... + ak can exceed n when the product of the factorials a1!, ..., ak! divides n! (n factorial, the product 1 x 2 x ... x n); decide whether, for every such k, the running total of g(1), ..., g(x) grows like a fixed constant times x times log x.

fermat_composite.title: Open questions about Fermat numbers — fermat_number_are_composite
fermat_composite.plain: Decide whether every Fermat number (2 raised to the power 2^n, plus 1) with n larger than 4 is composite, that is, not prime.

greens14.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 14 — green_14_polynomial
greens14.plain: W(k, r) is the smallest N such that, however the numbers 1 to N are coloured red and blue, there is a red evenly spaced run of k numbers or a blue evenly spaced run of r numbers; decide whether, for every k of at least 4, W(k, r) grows no faster than some fixed power of r.

infinite_fermat_primes.title: Open questions about Fermat numbers — infinite_fermat_primes
infinite_fermat_primes.plain: Decide whether infinitely many Fermat numbers (2 raised to the power 2^n, plus 1: 3, 5, 17, 257, 65537, ...) are prime.

pillai_conjecture.title: Catalan's conjecture and related Diophantine equations — pillais_conjecture
pillai_conjecture.plain: Show that, for any fixed positive whole numbers a, b and c, the equation a x^n - b y^m = c has only finitely many solutions with x, y, m and n all larger than 1 (leaving out m = n = 2).
